[Peter T. Tanksley]{.masthead-name}

[]{.belt-bar}

[Research Scientist, ALERRT Center · Texas State University]{.masthead-role}

::: {.masthead-thesis}
I study the people who run toward emergencies. Most of my work asks how the job of a first responder shapes health and mortality, mainly with national death-certificate data and biomarkers. The rest is about police: how they are trained to decide under pressure, and what the public makes of the decisions they end up making.
:::

<div class="eyebrow" style="margin-top:3.5rem">What I work on</div>

::: {.pillars}
::: {.pillar}
### First responder health and mortality
How law enforcement officers and firefighters die, and what in the work gets them there. Population-wide surveillance data, cardiometabolic biomarkers, and the policy that ought to follow from both.

[Read more →](research.qmd#health){.more}
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Police training and public opinion
How officers are trained to make high-stakes decisions, and how those decisions look to the public versus to the officers themselves. The two audiences disagree more often than either expects.

[Read more →](research.qmd#training){.more}
:::
:::
